Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
Value Name: Mature IXP ecosystem with broad participation
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: No source was cited for the original score (a plain claim_no_source case). Verified via PeeringDB, Hurricane Electric bgp.he.net and Packet Clearing House: Ghana has one active IXP, GIX, operated by the Ghana Internet Exchange Association (GIXA, est. 2005) in Accra, spanning four data-centre facilities (Digital Realty, Equinix AC1, NITA, ONIX) with 24-34 peering networks (including Google, Meta and Akamai) and roughly 214-224 Gbps aggregate capacity as of 2026. This is a genuine, active, moderately well-participated single exchange, but it is one IXP rather than a multi-hub national 'ecosystem' with broad participation on the scale of continental leaders (e.g. NAPAfrica, KIXP), so the code is revised down from 5 to 4 (Active IXP(s) with moderate participation).
